engine_info: Return the Protocol-major-1 engine descriptor before any workdir opens: protocol version, supported and required features, and the 53 tool names. Takes no arguments. Call it to discover capabilities or negotiate Protocol major 1. Do not use it to open or inspect a document; use workdir_open once you have a workdir.
workdir_open: Negotiate Protocol major 1 and open one validated typed workdir as the session document, reporting its freshness state and effective edit mode. Arguments: workdir (path to a directory containing typed.md), author (optional revision author, fallback $DOCX2TYPED_AUTHOR then "Unknown"), track (optional true/false to force tracked or direct edits; omitted infers from source_track_enabled and pending revisions), plus optional contract_ranges/supported_features/required_features for negotiation. Call it once before any document or review tool. It is the only tool that changes the session workdir. Do not use engine_info in place of opening a workdir.
workdir_status: Report the freshness state of the opened workdir: clean, dirty, stale-clean, or conflict. Takes no arguments. Use it to check whether the draft differs from the committed typed source before committing or reverting. It does not mutate anything and does not open a workdir; call workdir_open first.
list_paragraphs: List draft paragraphs with id, visible-text summary, token count, and deletions. Takes no arguments. Use it to enumerate paragraphs before addressing one by id. Read-only. For one paragraph's regions and formatting, use get_paragraph instead.
get_paragraph: Read one paragraph: its draft text and style regions. Argument: id (paragraph id, usually P0, P1, ...). The styles array is authoritative: equal style_id means identical formatting and rpr holds the full canonical run-properties XML. Use its regions to plan edits because replace_text rejects text crossing regions and batch_edit addresses regions by index. Use list_paragraphs first if you do not know the id. Read-only.
replace_text: Replace exactly one occurrence of visible text in a paragraph's draft. Arguments: paragraph_id, old (unique text, must fit one style region), new. Contract: old must be unique in the paragraph AND cover a single style region; crossing regions is rejected with the region boundaries, so edit each region separately. Style ownership is decided by the engine. Writes the draft only; run diff_preview then commit_sync. The mutating counterpart operation_id is appended by the engine via the mutation contract. Do not use it for multiple regions in one paragraph (use batch_edit), for whole-document replacements (use document_replace), or for handle-based edits (use facade_edit).
batch_edit: Edit several style regions of one paragraph atomically and immediately. Arguments: paragraph_id, edits (array of objects). Each edit targets one region, by index ({"region": 1, "new": "..."} or {"region": 2, "old": "...", "new": "..."}) or by text anchor ({"text": "...", "style_id": "...", "new": "..."}). Edits apply sequentially; if any fails the batch rolls back, and a region may be edited at most once per call. Use it instead of repeated replace_text when several regions of the same paragraph change. Do not use it across paragraphs (call once per paragraph).
insert_paragraph: Insert a new paragraph after after_id in the draft. Arguments: after_id, text, inherit (optional paragraph id whose insertion style to copy; defaults to after_id). Text is visible plain text; structural tokens are not allowed. In track mode the new paragraph carries a paragraph-mark insertion revision. Writes the draft only; commit later. Mutating. Do not use it to append prose inside an existing paragraph; use replace_text or batch_edit for that.
delete_paragraph: Delete a paragraph from the draft. Argument: paragraph_id. Paragraphs with protected structure (tokens, section boundaries) are rejected by commit_sync. In track mode the paragraph stays in the document with a paragraph-mark deletion revision. Writes the draft only. Do not use delete_comment here; comments are a different object addressed by w:id.
diff_preview: Dry-run of commit_sync: per changed paragraph, hunks with style ownership (source_style_set -> assigned_styles), warnings, or the rejection reason. Read-only; never mutates the workdir. Tracked hunks report their generated revisions. Takes no arguments. Run it before commit_sync to inspect the plan. Do not use workdir_status for the detailed hunk preview.
commit_sync: Apply the draft to the canonical typed AST and publish one CAS snapshot. Takes no arguments. Requires the workdir to be clean per commit. Mutating: requires an operation_id for replay/idempotency. Do not use revert, which discards the draft instead of publishing it.
accept_revision: Accept one tracked revision by its revision_key plus expected_fingerprint. Arguments: revision_key (part|kind|w:id|fingerprint from revisions.json), expected_fingerprint. Accept insert = unwrap its text; accept delete = remove it. Publishes transactionally and regenerates derived views; requires a clean workdir. For all revisions at once, use decide_all. Mutating with operation_id. Example: {"revision_key": "body|insert|3|abc", "expected_fingerprint": "abc", "operation_id": "accept-3"}.
reject_revision: Reject one tracked revision by revision_key + expected_fingerprint. Arguments: revision_key, expected_fingerprint. Reject insert = remove its text; reject delete = restore its text. Publishes transactionally; requires a clean workdir. For all revisions at once, use decide_all. Mutating with operation_id.
reinsert_deleted_text: Create a NEW insertion revision after an existing deletion identified by key + fingerprint, without touching the original deletion. Arguments: revision_key (or key), expected_fingerprint, text (defaults to the deleted text). Use it to restore deleted text as a new insertion rather than rejecting the deletion. Mutating with operation_id.
delete_comment: Delete one Word comment by its w:id: remove the comments.xml entry plus every commentRangeStart/End anchor and commentReference in the document. Arguments: comment_id (or id). Publishes transactionally; requires a clean workdir. Mutating with operation_id. Do not confuse with delete_paragraph, which removes body paragraphs.
table_insert_row: Insert an empty row after after (0-based) in table_ref (default T0). Arguments: table_ref, after, operation_id. Produces a new DOCX and a clean-baseline workdir; the source is untouched. Mutating with operation_id. Use table_insert_col for columns instead.
table_delete_row: Delete row row (0-based) from table_ref. Arguments: table_ref, row, operation_id. Mutating with operation_id. Use table_insert_row/table_insert_col for adding structure.
table_insert_col: Insert an empty column after after (0-based) in every row of table_ref. Arguments: table_ref, after, operation_id. Mutating with operation_id.
table_delete_col: Delete column col (0-based) from every row of table_ref. Arguments: table_ref, col, operation_id. Mutating with operation_id.
table_merge_cells: Merge span cells horizontally starting at (row, col) via gridSpan. Arguments: table_ref, row, col, span, discard_content (optional bool), operation_id. Fail-closed: if a spanned cell beyond the first carries text, the merge is refused with merge-would-discard-content unless discard_content=true explicitly drops it; the first cell's content is always kept. Mutating with operation_id. Example: {"table_ref": "T0", "row": 2, "col": 0, "span": 2, "operation_id": "merge-1"}.
table_split_cells: Split the cell at (row, col) into span cells. Arguments: table_ref, row, col, span, operation_id. Mutating with operation_id.
decide_all: Accept or reject every revision and produce a new clean-baseline project: build a decided DOCX at output and re-extract it into a new workdir at workdir_out. Arguments: action ("accept" or "reject"), output, workdir_out, operation_id. The original workdir is never mutated. Mutating with operation_id. Use accept_revision/reject_revision for a single revision.
list_comments: List every comment in the opened workdir: id, author, date, text, and the body paragraphs carrying its anchors. Takes no arguments. The comment workflow (delete_comment, decide_all) addresses comments by id. Read-only. For one comment, use get_comment.
get_comment: Read one comment: id, author, date, text, and the body paragraphs carrying its anchors. Argument: comment_id (or id). Read-only. Use list_comments if you do not know the id.
review_preflight: Return the agent gate, current snapshot, staged snapshot, and wake queue. Takes no arguments. Use it at the start of a review pass to learn what is actionable. Mutating context may be read; the tool itself is read-only for state. For collaboration session state without events, use review_state.
review_state: Read the collaboration session state without consuming review events. Takes no arguments. Read-only. Contrast with review_inbox, which reads queued events plus preflight, and review_preflight, which returns the agent gate.
review_external_preflight: Issue a CAS guard for an external import or rollback writer. Arguments: operation ("import" or "rollback"). It is the only tool whose operation argument accepts import/rollback; passing "document_patch" or any other string is rejected. Returns the common Result envelope; domain failures are isError Results with stable Diagnostics. Mutating (writes the guard).
review_settlement_plan: Return mixed accept/reject/defer decisions, patches, and carry-forward guards. Takes no arguments. Use it to plan settlement of review events. Run review_settle afterwards to atomically settle decisions.
review_settle: Atomically settle accept/reject decisions and carry deferred items. Arguments include the decisions and any deferred items (see schema). Mutating with operation_id: the id is mandatory because an empty event list means "whatever is actionable now", which changes between rounds. No stable default exists.
review_apply_patch: Apply the queued human patch batch containing event_id atomically. Arguments: event_id, operation_id (optional; when omitted the stable event-derived id "review-apply-patch-<event_id>" is used). Mutating with idempotent replay. Use review_apply_batch to apply a whole batch by batch_id.
review_apply_batch: Apply one queued human patch batch as one canonical transaction. Arguments: batch_id, operation_id (optional; when omitted uses "review-apply-batch-<batch_id>"). Mutating with idempotent replay.
review_inbox: Read queued review events together with the mandatory agent preflight. Takes no arguments. Use it to see new human input; then review_ack after consumption. Read-only. Contrast with review_state, which returns session state without events.
review_ack: Acknowledge review events after the agent has consumed them. Arguments: event identifiers as the schema requires. Mutating with operation_id; the id is mandatory because acking is caller-scoped consumption with no stable default.
revert: Discard the uncommitted draft and regenerate the projection from the canonical typed source (equivalent to edit refresh --discard). Takes no arguments. Mutating with operation_id. Use it to throw away draft changes; use commit_sync to publish them.
build_docx: Build the DOCX from the committed workdir, requiring clean state. Takes no arguments. Mutating with operation_id. Run verify_output afterwards to independently check the result. Do not use it on a dirty workdir.
verify_output: Independently verify a built DOCX against the workdir. Arguments: output (or path) to the built DOCX. Returns the common Result envelope with the verification result plus revision and comment summaries from the output package. An evidence publish failure reports the tool as failed. Run it after build_docx. Read-only with respect to the document.
history_list: Return the version timeline from HEAD backwards, newest first. Arguments: limit/offset as the schema supports. Read-only. Python reports draft freshness beside the store version_dirty in the same payload. Use history_diff or history_blame to drill into one version or paragraph.
history_gc: Run garbage collection over stale workdir versions/history. Arguments per schema. Mutating with operation_id. Requires a clean workdir. Use it to reclaim storage; it is not a revert of content.
history_restore: Restore the workdir state from a previous version. Arguments: version (required). Mutating with operation_id. Requires a clean workdir. Contrast with revert, which regenerates from the current canonical source rather than an older version.
document_search: Full-text search over the token-free edit projection. Arguments: query, context_chars (default 3000), case_sensitive (default false), limit (default 20), offset (default 0), scope (default "all"). Each match returns the enclosing paragraph block plus its match_ref, which you can pass directly to document_patch or format_span; search is the addressing layer. Read-only. Example: {"query": "smart response", "limit": 10}.
document_read: Read the editable projection as a virtual text file. Arguments: anchor, before (default 5), after (default 8), view (default "auto"). The content also serves as the diff base for document_patch, and revision is the token to pass as base_revision. Use it to inspect context before editing. Read-only.
document_patch: Apply a batch of hunks to the draft projection (low-level legacy transport for diffs). Arguments: hunks (array), diff (optional string), base_revision (from document_read), allow_comment_text (default false). Use it when you already have a structured diff/hunks. For simple find/replace edits prefer document_replace or, for handle-based edits, facade_edit/facade_resolve. Mutating (writes draft).
document_replace: Document-wide find/replace over the projection. Arguments: find, replace, scope (default "body"), regex (default false), case_sensitive (default true), expected_matches (optional), allow_comment_text (default false), base_revision (optional), dry_run (default false). Mutating unless dry_run. Use it instead of document_patch for string replacements. For editing from facade_locate handles use facade_edit.
history_diff: Show which paragraphs one version changed, against its parent by default. Arguments: version (required), against (optional parent version). Read-only. Use history_blame to find the version that last changed one paragraph.
history_blame: Report the version that last changed a given paragraph. Arguments: paragraph_id (or paragraph id per schema). Read-only. Use it to attribute changes before accepting or reverting.
history_verify: Verify the version store integrity. Takes no arguments. Read-only. Run it when you suspect corrupt history; it is not a document verification tool (use verify_output for that).
workspace_fork: Create a forked workdir/workspace from the current one. Arguments per schema (target path and optional branch/name). Mutating. Use it to experiment without touching the source workdir. workspace_adopt imports results back.
format_span: Change the formatting of existing text (the text-replacement lane cannot express formatting). Arguments: paragraph_id, old (copy verbatim from document_read), attributes (object such as {"vertAlign": "superscript"}) OR style_id, track (default false; tracked formatting is unsupported). Requires a clean draft and a clean workdir (format-requires-clean-draft). Mutating. Pass exactly one of attributes or style_id. Do not use it to change text; use replace_text for text.
workspace_adopt: Adopt an imported/child workdir's committed result back into the current workspace. Arguments per schema. Mutating with operation_id. Use it after workspace_fork or import workflows to commit the fork's changes. Run review_preflight before and verify_output after.
facade_locate: Find every occurrence with a stable, version-checked handle and a capability verdict, plus scanned coverage. Arguments: query, scope (default "body"). Read-only. Use its handles with facade_edit. The Facade is a thin composition over search/plan/verify and adds only agent-facing vocabulary (supported/unsupported/ambiguous/stale_revision) and a coverage block.
facade_edit: Apply handle-based edits (from facade_locate) in one call. Arguments: edits (array of {handle, replace_with}), dry_run (default false), track (optional), author, date. Use handles verbatim from facade_locate; do not invent {old,new} objects. When dry_run is true no changes are written. Mutating unless dry_run. It is the preferred replacement API over the legacy document_patch/document_replace when you have handles; it does not take base_revision because handles are version-checked. Example: {"edits": [{"handle": "h-12", "replace_with": "new text"}], "dry_run": true}.
facade_verify: Verify the result of a Facade edit pass. Arguments: query (optional), output (optional built DOCX path). Read-only with respect to the workdir. Use it to confirm supported/unsupported/ambiguous outcomes after facade_edit or facade_resolve.
facade_resolve: Resolve a find string to occurrences and edit them in one call. Arguments: find, replace_with, scope (default "body"), dry_run (default false), track (optional), author, date. It combines locate + edit internally. Mutating unless dry_run. Prefer it over document_replace when you want handle/version discipline and capability verdicts. Example: {"find": "smart response", "replace_with": "new text", "dry_run": true}.
